subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: After the registration-mode blocker is fixed, should OpenClaw accept `@openclaw/mxc-sandbox` as an official external plugin with `@microsoft/mxc-sdk` binaries, `node-pty`, and MXC's argv-carried base64 config transport?
rationale: This is a first-party sandbox and native dependency boundary; code review can identify the mechanics, but only maintainers/secops can decide whether that security posture is acceptable for an official plugin.

options.title: Accept after guard and exact-head dependency approval
options.body: Merge only after the non-full registration side effect is fixed and a maintainer/secops owner approves the final dependency graph and preview-SDK argv boundary.

options.title: Pause for upstream transport hardening
options.body: Keep the PR open but do not merge until MXC exposes a non-argv config transport or maintainers document why argv exposure is acceptable.

options.title: Keep MXC outside first-party packages
options.body: Close or redirect the work if official OpenClaw should not own a native Windows sandbox backend dependency at this stage.

recommendation.title: Accept after guard and exact-head dependency approval
recommendation.body: Merge only after the non-full registration side effect is fixed and a maintainer/secops owner approves the final dependency graph and preview-SDK argv boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` is the current assignee and has the clearest sandbox-backend history through OpenShell and SSH sandbox work.
